title: Beyond Pairwise Repulsion: Collective Diversity via Determinant Maximization in Diffusion Sampling

paper.title: Beyond Pairwise Repulsion: Collective Diversity via Determinant Maximization in Diffusion Sampling
paper.abstract:
Abstract Strong guidance in text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models concentrates sampling toward high-density modes of the conditional distribution, collapsing independently sampled noise vectors onto nearly identical visual prototypes.
This limits utility for tasks that demand distributional breadth, most critically synthetic data augmentation.
Diversity, however, is a collective property of the whole batch: a set can preserve every pairwise distance yet still collapse onto a low-dimensional subspace.
Existing sum-of-pairwise noise-optimization and repulsion objectives respond only weakly to this higher-order failure.
We propose DetNO ( Det erminant N oise O ptimization), which formulates diverse generation as RKHS volume maximization on the initial noise, maximizing the log-determinant of an RBF Gram matrix over one-step Tweedie predictions.
This set-level functional equals the squared batch volume; its repulsion is strongest when the batch is most collapsed and self-attenuates as diversity is achieved.
An anchor-based fidelity term keeps the optimized noises near plausible regions, and Lagrangian relaxation gives a two-term objective with a single hyperparameter λ \lambda governing the diversity–quality trade-off, without training or sampler modification.
Across three backbones (SD1.5, SDXL, SD3), DetNO achieves leading intra-batch diversity in VendiScore and Mean Self-Similarity, and a downstream few-shot classification experiment confirms that broader mode coverage brings statistically significant accuracy gains for synthetic data augmentation in the low-shot regime.
Fixing the pipeline and varying only the batch objective, both RBF-based aggregators outperform InfoNCE, and the log-determinant attains the best downstream accuracy on both benchmarks.
Its diversity advantage over InfoNCE widens as the batch grows.
Code is available at https://github.com/mobled37/DetNO .

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) [ 12 ] has become the standard mechanism for steering text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models [ 11 , 27 , 24 ] toward high-fidelity, prompt-aligned images. Strong CFG, however, concentrates sampling toward the high-density peak of the conditional distribution, collapsing its effective support onto a narrow region of the image manifold (Fig. 1 ). Under deterministic samplers such as DDIM [ 26 ] , the initial noise fully determines the final image, yet independent noise draws collapse onto the same narrow visual mode. Multiple images generated from the same prompt converge to nearly identical visual prototypes. The collapse limits utility in applications that depend on distributional breadth, most critically synthetic data augmentation, where near-duplicate outputs provide diminishing returns for downstream model training [ 9 ] . Recovering this diversity requires treating a batch as a whole, since diversity is a collective property of the set rather than a sum over its pairs. A batch can preserve every pairwise distance yet still collapse onto a low-dimensional subspace, a higher-order failure mode to which independent pair contributions respond only weakly. Existing approaches meet this criterion only partially. Methods that intervene during denoising repel intermediate latents [ 3 , 14 ] or manipulate text embeddings [ 31 ] , paying a per-step cost that scales with trajectory length. Contrastive Noise Optimization (CNO) [ 13 ] instead optimizes the initial noise with an InfoNCE loss in the Tweedie prediction space, intervening before denoising begins, where the noise largely determines semantic structure [ 8 , 2 ] . Despite their differing entry points, all build their diversity signal from sum-of-pairwise repulsion, whose gradient remains confined to the span of pairwise directions and can miss higher-order redundancy. This motivates a single scalar measuring the collective volume a batch occupies, penalizing redundancy at every order up to B B simultaneously. We realize this scalar as the log-determinant of an RBF Gram matrix over one-step Tweedie predictions, making all-order diversity differentiable. We further show that this objective is self-regulating: repulsion amplifies when the batch is most redundant and relaxes as diversity is achieved, an adaptation that an unweighted sum-of-pairwise objective lacks in the same analysis. Figure 2 : Conceptual illustration of DetNO. (a) Strong CFG guidance concentrates sampling toward the high-density peak, leaving the degrees of freedom in the initial noise unexploited. DetNO recovers this freedom by optimizing the initial noise batch to reach low-density regions that standard sampling cannot access. (b) The diversity term (green) maximizes the RKHS volume collectively spanned by all Tweedie predictions, while the fidelity term (yellow) regularizes each sample toward its unoptimized reference, expanding distributional coverage while preserving prompt fidelity. We propose DetNO ( Det erminant N oise O ptimization), illustrated in Fig. 2 , which pairs this log-determinant diversity term with an anchor-based fidelity term via Lagrangian relaxation. A single hyperparameter λ \lambda controls the diversity-quality trade-off, with no training or sampler modification. Empirically, the collective objective delivers on both diversity and downstream utility. Across three backbones (SD1.5, SDXL, SD3), DetNO achieves leading intra-batch diversity in VendiScore and Mean Self-Similarity, with the advantage over CNO widening as the batch size grows. A controlled toy experiment shows faithful recovery of all modes where pairwise methods distort mode structure, and downstream few-shot classification produces accuracy gains over both standard sampling and CNO, reaching statistical significance in the low-shot regime ( p < 0.01 p{<}0.01 ). Our main contributions are as follows: • We recast diverse T2I generation as a set-level rather than pairwise problem: constrained RKHS volume maximization on initial noise. The objective pairs a log-determinant diversity term with an anchor-based fidelity term, controlled by a single hyperparameter λ \lambda , with no sampler modification. • We show that the log-determinant amplifies repulsion when the batch is most redundant and relaxes as diversity is achieved, a self-regulating property of the Gram matrix eigenspectrum that an unweighted sum-of-pairwise objective lacks in the same analysis. • We validate across three backbone-sampler configurations, demonstrating consistent diversity gains with a controllable quality-diversity trade-off and statistically significant downstream improvements in few-shot classification.

sections.heading: 2.1 Recovering Mode Diversity in Diffusion Models.
sections.text: Prior methods recover the limited diversity of conditional diffusion models through repulsion, differing mainly in where they apply it but sharing a diversity signal that decomposes into a sum of pairwise interactions. One line intervenes during denoising: SPELL [ 14 ] adds sparse repellency terms to the reverse SDE, Particle Guidance (PG) [ 3 ] repels intermediate latents via a joint-particle potential, and DiversityPrompt [ 31 ] optimizes a token embedding online to steer generation toward low-density regions. All incur per-step overhead that scales with trajectory length. Contrastive Noise Optimization (CNO) [ 13 ] instead shifts repulsion to the initial noise, optimizing latents via InfoNCE in the Tweedie prediction space before sampling begins. Both, however, quantify diversity as a sum over sample pairs, so their repulsion never leaves the span of pairwise directions and responds only weakly to higher-order redundancy that collapses the batch onto a low-dimensional subspace. A separate line targets rare modes of the unconditional or class-conditional distribution via classifier guidance [ 25 , 29 ] , self-guided sampling [ 30 ] , or modified noise schedules [ 28 ] . Our goal instead is to recover suppressed modes of a text-conditional distribution under strong guidance for a fixed prompt.

sections.heading: 2.2 Initial Noise Optimization in Diffusion Models.
sections.text: InitNO [ 8 ] steers noise toward valid regions via attention-based scores for better text adherence, while [ 2 ] learn a mapping to optimal noise configurations to characterize CFG behavior. Neither addresses diversity. CNO [ 13 ] establishes that optimizing the initial noise alone can recover suppressed modes, using a pairwise contrastive objective. We inherit this noise-space pipeline from CNO; what changes is the structure of the diversity signal, from a sum over pairs to log-determinant maximization, a set-level functional equal to the squared RKHS volume that penalizes redundancy at every order. This objective is jointly optimized with an anchor-based fidelity term under a single hyperparameter λ \lambda . The log-determinant as a diversity criterion originates in GDPP [ 4 ] , which regularizes a GAN’s generator with a DPP kernel. We instead apply it as an inference-time objective on the Tweedie predictions of a frozen diffusion model, requiring no training and no DPP sampling.

sections.heading: 3.1 Tweedie’s Formula and Clean Data Estimation
sections.text: Diffusion models generate data by iteratively denoising a Gaussian noise sample z T ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 𝟎 , 𝐈 ) z_{T}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}) through a learned reverse process. At each timestep t t , a noisy latent z t z_{t} is related to the clean data z 0 z_{0} via the forward process z t = α ¯ t ​ z 0 + 1 − α ¯ t ​ ϵ z_{t}=\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_{t}}\,z_{0}+\sqrt{1-\bar{\alpha}_{t}}\,\epsilon , where ϵ ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 𝟎 , 𝐈 ) \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}) and α ¯ t ≔ ∏ i = 1 t α i \bar{\alpha}_{t}\coloneqq\prod_{i=1}^{t}\alpha_{i} is the cumulative noise schedule. A neural network ϵ θ ​ ( z t , t , c ) \epsilon_{\theta}(z_{t},t,c) is trained to predict the noise ϵ \epsilon given the noisy observation z t z_{t} , timestep t t , and text conditioning c c . Tweedie’s formula [ 23 ] provides a closed-form estimate of the posterior mean 𝔼 ⁡ [ z 0 ∣ z t ] \mathbb{E}[z_{0}\mid z_{t}] , yielding a one-step prediction of the clean latent at any timestep: z ^ 0 | t ​ ( z t , t , c ) ≔ 1 α ¯ t ​ ( z t − 1 − α ¯ t ​ ϵ θ ​ ( z t , t , c ) ) . \hat{z}_{0|t}(z_{t},t,c)\coloneqq\frac{1}{\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_{t}}}\left(z_{t}-\sqrt{1-\bar{\alpha}_{t}}\,\epsilon_{\theta}(z_{t},t,c)\right). (1) This estimate represents the model’s best prediction of the clean data given the current noisy observation. While the prediction becomes increasingly accurate as t → 0 t\to 0 , even at the initial timestep T T it captures meaningful semantic structure of the final generation, such as global layout and dominant color [ 2 ] . Our method exploits this property by operating entirely in the Tweedie prediction space at t = T t=T , optimizing the initial noises to diversify their corresponding clean data estimates before any denoising takes place.

sections.text: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) [ 12 ] enhances text-image alignment by interpolating between the conditional and unconditional noise predictions: ϵ ^ β ​ ( z t , t , c ) = ( 1 + β ) ​ ϵ θ ​ ( z t , t , c ) − β ​ ϵ θ ​ ( z t , t , ∅ ) , \hat{\epsilon}_{\beta}(z_{t},t,c)=(1+\beta)\,\epsilon_{\theta}(z_{t},t,c)-\beta\,\epsilon_{\theta}(z_{t},t,\varnothing), (2) where β > 0 \beta>0 is the guidance scale and ∅ \varnothing denotes the null condition. sections.heading: 4.2 Diversity: RKHS Volume Maximization
sections.text: As motivated in Sec. 1 , we quantify diversity as the volume a batch collectively occupies, a set-level functional that penalizes redundancy at every order simultaneously. An unweighted pairwise sum, by contrast, yields a gradient confined to the span of pairwise directions. Realizing this in the Tweedie prediction space requires care: the raw prediction z ^ 0 | T i ∈ ℝ C × H × W \hat{z}_{0|T}^{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times H\times W} suffers from norm concentration, where pairwise distances between independent samples converge to a common value [ 1 ] . This drives the RBF kernel toward a constant, flattening the very volume signal we maximize. Predictions at t = T t{=}T primarily encode coarse semantic layout rather than fine spatial detail [ 2 ] . We therefore suppress high-frequency variance via adaptive average pooling with window w w , then project onto the unit hypersphere: z ~ 0 | T i = AvgPool ⁡ ( z ^ 0 | T i , w ) , z ¯ 0 | T i = z ~ 0 | T i / ‖ z ~ 0 | T i ‖ 2 , \tilde{z}_{0|T}^{i}=\mathrm{AvgPool}(\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i},\;w),\qquad\bar{z}_{0|T}^{i}=\tilde{z}_{0|T}^{i}\big/\|\tilde{z}_{0|T}^{i}\|_{2}, (3) producing compact representations z ¯ 0 | T i ∈ ℝ C ​ w 2 \bar{z}_{0|T}^{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{Cw^{2}} on which kernel similarities reflect semantic structure rather than high-frequency noise. sections.heading: 4.3 Fidelity: Anchor-Based Displacement Constraint
sections.text: Volume maximization alone would push noise vectors into out-of-distribution regions. Since CFG concentrates p β ​ ( z 0 ∣ c ) ∝ p ⁡ ( z 0 ) ​ p ​ ( c ∣ z 0 ) β p_{\beta}(z_{0}\mid c)\propto p(z_{0})\,p(c\mid z_{0})^{\beta} around high-density modes, each reference prediction z ^ 0 | T i , ref \hat{z}_{0|T}^{i,\mathrm{ref}} from the unoptimized noise lies near a high-density region of the sharpened posterior by construction. We regularize displacement from these anchors in the full-resolution prediction space: ‖ z ^ 0 | T i − z ^ 0 | T i , ref ‖ 2 ≤ δ , ∀ i ∈ { 1 , … , B } . \left\|\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i}-\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i,\mathrm{ref}}\right\|^{2}\leq\delta,\quad\forall\,i\in\{1,\dots,B\}. (8) The constrained problem is therefore: min Z T − log det ( S + ϵ I ) s . t . ‖ z ^ 0 | T i − z ^ 0 | T i , ref ‖ 2 ≤ δ , ∀ i ∈ { 1 , … , B } . \min_{Z_{T}}\;-\log\det(S+\epsilon I)\quad\mathrm{s.t.}\quad\left\|\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i}-\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i,\mathrm{ref}}\right\|^{2}\leq\delta,\quad\forall\,i\in\{1,\dots,B\}. (9) Introducing per-sample Lagrange multipliers { λ i } i = 1 B \{\lambda_{i}\}_{i=1}^{B} ( λ i ≥ 0 \lambda_{i}\geq 0 ) gives the Lagrangian: ℒ = − log det ( S + ϵ I ) + ∑ i = 1 B λ i ( ‖ z ^ 0 | T i − z ^ 0 | T i , ref ‖ 2 − δ ) . \mathcal{L}=-\log\det(S+\epsilon I)+\sum_{i=1}^{B}\lambda_{i}\left(\left\|\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i}-\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i,\mathrm{ref}}\right\|^{2}-\delta\right). (10) As a practical simplification, since all B B samples are drawn from the same prompt, backbone, and noise prior, we use a single shared multiplier λ \lambda across all samples and absorb the constant − λ ​ B ​ δ -\lambda B\delta into λ \lambda , arriving at the final objective: ℒ = − log det ( S + ϵ I ) ⏟ Diversity + λ ​ ∑ i = 1 B ‖ z ^ 0 | T i − z ^ 0 | T i , ref ‖ 2 ⏟ Fidelity \boxed{\mathcal{L}=\underbrace{-\log\det(S+\epsilon I)}_{\text{Diversity}}+\underbrace{\lambda\sum_{i=1}^{B}\left\|\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i}-\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i,\mathrm{ref}}\right\|^{2}}_{\text{Fidelity}}} (11) where ϵ > 0 \epsilon>0 ensures numerical stability. The two terms are fully decoupled: diversity depends on pooled, normalized representations, while fidelity operates on unpooled predictions at full spatial resolution. A single hyperparameter λ \lambda transparently controls the trade-off, with no sampler modification required. Following [ 13 ] , we apply a stop-gradient operator on the UNet output when computing Tweedie predictions. This eliminates the need to store UNet activations during backpropagation, reducing GPU memory to the level of standard inference. Algorithm 1 summarizes the full procedure.

sections.text: Figure 3 : Toy example on a 2D ring mixture with 8 inner modes (80%) and 8 outer modes (20%). (a) Ground truth distribution. (b) Classifier-free guidance collapses onto the majority inner ring, without covering outer modes. (c) CNO recovers the outer modes but severely distorts the inner ring, producing only 4 inner modes whose sample distributions no longer align with the ground truth geometry. (d) DetNO achieves full coverage of all 16 modes across both rings, faithfully preserving the original mode structure.

sections.heading: Implementation Details.
sections.text: We evaluate on three pre-trained T2I backbones: SD1.5 [ 24 ] , SDXL [ 22 ] , and SD3 [ 5 ] . SD1.5 and SDXL use DDIM [ 26 ] with 50 steps, while SD3 uses the Euler sampler with 28 steps following its default configuration. We compare against PG [ 3 ] , SPELL [ 14 ] , DiversityPrompt [ 31 ] , and CNO [ 13 ] . We evaluate all methods under identical conditions (prompt set, random seeds, CFG scale, and hardware) to ensure fair relative comparison; absolute values may differ from original papers accordingly. We use the official implementations of all baselines, including CNO, with the hyperparameters reported in their original papers. Following [ 31 , 13 ] , we sample 2,000 prompts from the MS-COCO [ 18 ] validation set and generate 5 images per prompt for SD1.5 and SD3, and 3 images per prompt for SDXL.

sections.heading: Evaluation Metrics.
sections.text: For image quality, we report Precision [ 17 ] , Density [ 19 ] , CLIPScore [ 10 ] , PickScore [ 15 ] , and ImageReward [ 33 ] . For diversity, we report Recall [ 17 ] , Coverage [ 19 ] , Vendi Score [ 6 ] , and Mean Self-Similarity (MSS) [ 13 ] . Among these, VendiScore and MSS serve as our primary diversity metrics, as they measure intra-batch coverage directly without reference to an external distribution. They are therefore better suited to evaluating diversity-enhancing methods than reference-dependent metrics such as Recall and Coverage [ 20 ] .

sections.heading: Toy Example: 2D Ring Mixture.
sections.text: Only the log-determinant preserves the full mode structure in a controlled setting, a 2D ring mixture with 8 inner modes (80%) and 8 outer modes (20%) ( Fig. 3 ). CFG (b) collapses onto the majority inner ring, CNO (c) recovers the outer ring while distorting the inner one, and DetNO (d) covers all 16 modes. The two failures are distinct: CFG cannot reach the suppressed modes at all, while InfoNCE-style contrastive repulsion reaches them but keeps pushing after samples are already separated, distorting the geometry it recovers. The log-determinant instead self-attenuates as volume is restored ( Proposition 1 ), separating samples without displacing the modes themselves. Figure 4 : Qualitative comparison on SD1.5. For each prompt, we show one representative sample from DDIM, CNO, and DetNO (ours). DDIM and CNO produce visually near-identical outputs across seeds, differing only in minor details such as slight pose or hair difference. DetNO generates substantially different images, varying in viewpoint, object appearance, scene layout, and human identity, while remaining faithful to the prompt. sections.heading: Quantitative Results.
sections.text: DetNO achieves the best MSS and VendiScore on all three (SD1.5, SDXL, SD3) in Tab. 1 , confirming systematic diversity gains across all three backbones and both samplers tested (DDIM and Euler). CNO also improves diversity, but its VendiScore gain over the baseline is roughly half of DetNO’s on each backbone. On reference-free quality metrics (PickScore, ImageReward), the trade-off is small: PickScore decreases only marginally on every backbone, while ImageReward matches the baseline on SD1.5 and decreases modestly on SDXL and SD3. Reference-dependent metrics (Precision, Density, Coverage) decrease accordingly, as they reward overlap with the narrow MS-COCO reference set [ 20 ] rather than per-image quality. The trade-off remains controllable: the Pareto analysis ( Fig. 5 ) shows λ \lambda smoothly interpolating between the two objectives, and on its 200-prompt sweep every tested SD3 configuration improves over the baseline on CLIPScore, PickScore, and ImageReward; under the full 2,000-prompt protocol, the deployed configuration trades a small amount of PickScore and ImageReward for its diversity gains ( Tab. 1 ).

sections.heading: Qualitative Results.
sections.text: The diversity gains are plainly visible ( Fig. 4 , six SD1.5 prompts; SDXL and SD3 examples in Figs. S1 and S2 ). DDIM and CNO are nearly indistinguishable, sharing global layout, object placement, and dominant color palette across all examples. DetNO instead varies object identity, viewpoint, and scene composition while remaining prompt-faithful, recovering degrees of freedom in the initial noise that standard sampling and pairwise objectives leave unexploited.

sections.heading: Downstream Classification.
sections.text: These diversity gains translate into practical utility. We evaluate synthetic data augmentation in a few-shot classification setting using two fine-grained benchmarks: Oxford-IIIT Pets (37 breeds) [ 21 ] with SD3 and CUB-200-2011 (200 species) [ 32 ] with SD1.5. For each class, we generate 16 synthetic images and combine them with K K -shot real images to fine-tune a pretrained ResNet-18 (Tab. 2 ). DetNO consistently outperforms both DDIM and CNO across both datasets, with gains most pronounced in the low-data regime: + 2.0 +2.0 pp at 1-shot on Pets and + 1.7 +1.7 pp on CUB-200 over DDIM, where distributional breadth of synthetic data is directly impactful. CNO remains within noise of DDIM on both datasets, whereas DetNO’s broader mode coverage provides tangible downstream benefits beyond what diversity metrics alone would suggest. The log-determinant attains the best intra-batch diversity, and both RBF-based aggregators outperform InfoNCE. Because the pairwise-RBF and log-determinant rows differ only in aggregating S S additively versus through its determinant, the comparison isolates the aggregation structure. The gap at B = 5 B{=}5 is small, as expected where higher-order redundancies are few; most of the gain over InfoNCE comes from the shared RBF kernel and fidelity design. We report intra-batch diversity for comparability but treat downstream accuracy as decisive. sections.heading: Ablation study on the loss components.
sections.text: Both loss terms are necessary: Tab. 4 isolates each term’s contribution on SD1.5. The diversity term alone (A) achieves the strongest diversity but at substantial quality cost, pushing noise vectors into out-of-distribution regions (bottom row of Fig. 6 ). The fidelity term alone (B) preserves quality but provides no diversity improvement. The full objective (A+B) recovers most diversity gains while maintaining prompt-faithful outputs (middle row of Fig. 6 ).

sections.heading: Scaling with batch size.
sections.text: All-order and pairwise objectives coincide at B = 2 B\!=\!2 and diverge only as higher-order redundancies accumulate; we therefore sweep B ∈ { 3 , 5 , 8 , 12 , 16 } B\in\{3,5,8,12,16\} on SD1.5 with all else fixed ( Fig. 7 ). Both methods improve over DDIM, but DetNO’s advantage over CNO is marginal at small B B and widens monotonically as B B grows. The trend is consistent with the all-order argument: a pairwise objective sees only the ( B 2 ) \binom{B}{2} pair terms, while the higher-order redundancies the log-determinant penalizes grow combinatorially with B B . As the two methods also differ in kernel and fidelity design, the gap reflects their combined effect. Its gradient adds an O ⁡ ( B 3 ) O(B^{3}) matrix factorization per step, negligible against the B B denoiser evaluations that dominate each iteration. Synthetic data augmentation operates in exactly this large-batch regime.

sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: We presented DetNO, an initial-noise optimization framework that maximizes the RKHS volume among Tweedie predictions via a log-determinant diversity term and an anchor-based fidelity term. Experiments on SD1.5, SDXL, and SD3 confirm consistent diversity gains across backbones and samplers, with Pareto analysis showing that λ \lambda enables smooth interpolation between the two objectives. A toy experiment and a spectral analysis ( Proposition 1 ) trace this advantage to its mechanism: repulsion that intensifies where the batch is most collapsed and relaxes once diversity is restored. In downstream few-shot classification, the broader mode coverage translates into statistically significant accuracy gains in the low-data regime. Treating diversity as a property of the whole batch, rather than of its pairs, thus produces image sets that are not only more varied but measurably more useful.

sections.text: As shown in Table S6 , stop-gradient already yields clear diversity gains over the baseline (MSS, VendiScore) at a marginal quality cost. Full gradient achieves moderately stronger gains (particularly in Recall and VendiScore) by propagating richer second-order information through the denoising network, but at the cost of storing all intermediate UNet activations during backpropagation. sections.heading: 0.A.9 Ablation on Noise Scale
sections.text: To validate that the diversity gains of DetNO cannot be replicated by simply scaling the initial noise variance, we evaluate 𝐳 T ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 𝟎 , s 2 ​ 𝐈 ) \mathbf{z}_{T}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},s^{2}\mathbf{I}) across a range of scale values s s on SD1.5. As shown in Tab. S7 , any deviation from the standard s = 1 s=1 causes severe image degradation across all quality metrics. At s = 0.5 s=0.5 , Recall collapses to 0.0002 0.0002 and ImageReward drops to − 2.28 -2.28 , indicating that the denoiser operates far outside its training distribution and produces degenerate outputs. Increasing the scale to s ≥ 1.2 s\geq 1.2 yields similarly catastrophic failures: Recall falls below 0.04 0.04 , CLIPScore drops by more than 8 8 points, and ImageReward becomes strongly negative across all configurations. This behavior is expected: diffusion model denoisers are trained exclusively with s = 1 s=1 , and any perturbation to the noise scale pushes the initial latent out of the distribution seen during training, causing the reverse process to produce corrupted images regardless of the direction of the scale change. These results confirm that noise scale manipulation is not a viable mechanism for diversity enhancement, and that the diversity gains of DetNO arise from structured optimization within the valid noise distribution rather than from distributional shift. This limits utility for tasks that demand distributional breadth, most critically synthetic data augmentation. Diversity, however, is a collective property of the whole batch: a set can preserve every pairwise distance yet still collapse onto a low-dimensional subspace. Existing sum-of-pairwise noise-optimization and repulsion objectives respond only weakly to this higher-order failure. We propose DetNO ( Det erminant N oise O ptimization), which formulates diverse generation as RKHS volume maximization on the initial noise, maximizing the log-determinant of an RBF Gram matrix over one-step Tweedie predictions. This set-level functional equals the squared batch volume; its repulsion is strongest when the batch is most collapsed and self-attenuates as diversity is achieved. An anchor-based fidelity term keeps the optimized noises near plausible regions, and Lagrangian relaxation gives a two-term objective with a single hyperparameter λ \lambda governing the diversity–quality trade-off, without training or sampler modification. Across three backbones (SD1.5, SDXL, SD3), DetNO achieves leading intra-batch diversity in VendiScore and Mean Self-Similarity, and a downstream few-shot classification experiment confirms that broader mode coverage brings statistically significant accuracy gains for synthetic data augmentation in the low-shot regime. Fixing the pipeline and varying only the batch objective, both RBF-based aggregators outperform InfoNCE, and the log-determinant attains the best downstream accuracy on both benchmarks. Its diversity advantage over InfoNCE widens as the batch grows. Code is available at https://github.com/mobled37/DetNO . Keywords: Text-to-Image Diffusion Models Diverse Image Generation Initial Noise Optimization Log-Determinant Maximization Synthetic Data Augmentation Figure 1 : Qualitative comparison on SD3. SD3 baseline sampling collapses onto a narrow visual prototype for underspecified prompts, reproducing nearly identical appearance and scene layout across seeds, a direct consequence of CFG concentrating the conditional distribution onto its high-density peak. DetNO recovers the suppressed degrees of freedom in initial noise, producing semantically diverse outputs that vary in viewpoint, identity, clothes, and scene composition while remaining faithful to the prompt. 1 Introduction Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) [ 12 ] has become the standard mechanism for steering text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models [ 11 , 27 , 24 ] toward high-fidelity, prompt-aligned images. Strong CFG, however, concentrates sampling toward the high-density peak of the conditional distribution, collapsing its effective support onto a narrow region of the image manifold (Fig. 1 ). Under deterministic samplers such as DDIM [ 26 ] , the initial noise fully determines the final image, yet independent noise draws collapse onto the same narrow visual mode. Multiple images generated from the same prompt converge to nearly identical visual prototypes. The collapse limits utility in applications that depend on distributional breadth, most critically synthetic data augmentation, where near-duplicate outputs provide diminishing returns for downstream model training [ 9 ] . Recovering this diversity requires treating a batch as a whole, since diversity is a collective property of the set rather than a sum over its pairs. A batch can preserve every pairwise distance yet still collapse onto a low-dimensional subspace, a higher-order failure mode to which independent pair contributions respond only weakly. Existing approaches meet this criterion only partially. Methods that intervene during denoising repel intermediate latents [ 3 , 14 ] or manipulate text embeddings [ 31 ] , paying a per-step cost that scales with trajectory length. Contrastive Noise Optimization (CNO) [ 13 ] instead optimizes the initial noise with an InfoNCE loss in the Tweedie prediction space, intervening before denoising begins, where the noise largely determines semantic structure [ 8 , 2 ] . Despite their differing entry points, all build their diversity signal from sum-of-pairwise repulsion, whose gradient remains confined to the span of pairwise directions and can miss higher-order redundancy. This motivates a single scalar measuring the collective volume a batch occupies, penalizing redundancy at every order up to B B simultaneously. We realize this scalar as the log-determinant of an RBF Gram matrix over one-step Tweedie predictions, making all-order diversity differentiable. We further show that this objective is self-regulating: repulsion amplifies when the batch is most redundant and relaxes as diversity is achieved, an adaptation that an unweighted sum-of-pairwise objective lacks in the same analysis. Figure 2 : Conceptual illustration of DetNO. (a) Strong CFG guidance concentrates sampling toward the high-density peak, leaving the degrees of freedom in the initial noise unexploited. DetNO recovers this freedom by optimizing the initial noise batch to reach low-density regions that standard sampling cannot access. (b) The diversity term (green) maximizes the RKHS volume collectively spanned by all Tweedie predictions, while the fidelity term (yellow) regularizes each sample toward its unoptimized reference, expanding distributional coverage while preserving prompt fidelity. We propose DetNO ( Det erminant N oise O ptimization), illustrated in Fig. 2 , which pairs this log-determinant diversity term with an anchor-based fidelity term via Lagrangian relaxation. A single hyperparameter λ \lambda controls the diversity-quality trade-off, with no training or sampler modification. Empirically, the collective objective delivers on both diversity and downstream utility. Across three backbones (SD1.5, SDXL, SD3), DetNO achieves leading intra-batch diversity in VendiScore and Mean Self-Similarity, with the advantage over CNO widening as the batch size grows. A controlled toy experiment shows faithful recovery of all modes where pairwise methods distort mode structure, and downstream few-shot classification produces accuracy gains over both standard sampling and CNO, reaching statistical significance in the low-shot regime ( p < 0.01 p{<}0.01 ). Our main contributions are as follows: • We recast diverse T2I generation as a set-level rather than pairwise problem: constrained RKHS volume maximization on initial noise. The objective pairs a log-determinant diversity term with an anchor-based fidelity term, controlled by a single hyperparameter λ \lambda , with no sampler modification. • We show that the log-determinant amplifies repulsion when the batch is most redundant and relaxes as diversity is achieved, a self-regulating property of the Gram matrix eigenspectrum that an unweighted sum-of-pairwise objective lacks in the same analysis. • We validate across three backbone-sampler configurations, demonstrating consistent diversity gains with a controllable quality-diversity trade-off and statistically significant downstream improvements in few-shot classification. 2 Related Work 2.1 Recovering Mode Diversity in Diffusion Models. Prior methods recover the limited diversity of conditional diffusion models through repulsion, differing mainly in where they apply it but sharing a diversity signal that decomposes into a sum of pairwise interactions. One line intervenes during denoising: SPELL [ 14 ] adds sparse repellency terms to the reverse SDE, Particle Guidance (PG) [ 3 ] repels intermediate latents via a joint-particle potential, and DiversityPrompt [ 31 ] optimizes a token embedding online to steer generation toward low-density regions. All incur per-step overhead that scales with trajectory length. Contrastive Noise Optimization (CNO) [ 13 ] instead shifts repulsion to the initial noise, optimizing latents via InfoNCE in the Tweedie prediction space before sampling begins. Both, however, quantify diversity as a sum over sample pairs, so their repulsion never leaves the span of pairwise directions and responds only weakly to higher-order redundancy that collapses the batch onto a low-dimensional subspace. A separate line targets rare modes of the unconditional or class-conditional distribution via classifier guidance [ 25 , 29 ] , self-guided sampling [ 30 ] , or modified noise schedules [ 28 ] . Our goal instead is to recover suppressed modes of a text-conditional distribution under strong guidance for a fixed prompt. 2.2 Initial Noise Optimization in Diffusion Models. InitNO [ 8 ] steers noise toward valid regions via attention-based scores for better text adherence, while [ 2 ] learn a mapping to optimal noise configurations to characterize CFG behavior. Neither addresses diversity. CNO [ 13 ] establishes that optimizing the initial noise alone can recover suppressed modes, using a pairwise contrastive objective. We inherit this noise-space pipeline from CNO; what changes is the structure of the diversity signal, from a sum over pairs to log-determinant maximization, a set-level functional equal to the squared RKHS volume that penalizes redundancy at every order. This objective is jointly optimized with an anchor-based fidelity term under a single hyperparameter λ \lambda . The log-determinant as a diversity criterion originates in GDPP [ 4 ] , which regularizes a GAN’s generator with a DPP kernel. We instead apply it as an inference-time objective on the Tweedie predictions of a frozen diffusion model, requiring no training and no DPP sampling. 3 Preliminaries 3.1 Tweedie’s Formula and Clean Data Estimation Diffusion models generate data by iteratively denoising a Gaussian noise sample z T ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 𝟎 , 𝐈 ) z_{T}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}) through a learned reverse process. At each timestep t t , a noisy latent z t z_{t} is related to the clean data z 0 z_{0} via the forward process z t = α ¯ t ​ z 0 + 1 − α ¯ t ​ ϵ z_{t}=\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_{t}}\,z_{0}+\sqrt{1-\bar{\alpha}_{t}}\,\epsilon , where ϵ ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 𝟎 , 𝐈 ) \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}) and α ¯ t ≔ ∏ i = 1 t α i \bar{\alpha}_{t}\coloneqq\prod_{i=1}^{t}\alpha_{i} is the cumulative noise schedule. Tweedie’s formula [ 23 ] provides a closed-form estimate of the posterior mean 𝔼 ⁡ [ z 0 ∣ z t ] \mathbb{E}[z_{0}\mid z_{t}] , yielding a one-step prediction of the clean latent at any timestep: z ^ 0 | t ​ ( z t , t , c ) ≔ 1 α ¯ t ​ ( z t − 1 − α ¯ t ​ ϵ θ ​ ( z t , t , c ) ) . \hat{z}_{0|t}(z_{t},t,c)\coloneqq\frac{1}{\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_{t}}}\left(z_{t}-\sqrt{1-\bar{\alpha}_{t}}\,\epsilon_{\theta}(z_{t},t,c)\right). (1) This estimate represents the model’s best prediction of the clean data given the current noisy observation. While the prediction becomes increasingly accurate as t → 0 t\to 0 , even at the initial timestep T T it captures meaningful semantic structure of the final generation, such as global layout and dominant color [ 2 ] . Our method exploits this property by operating entirely in the Tweedie prediction space at t = T t=T , optimizing the initial noises to diversify their corresponding clean data estimates before any denoising takes place. 3.2 Classifier-Free Guidance Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) [ 12 ] enhances text-image alignment by interpolating between the conditional and unconditional noise predictions: ϵ ^ β ​ ( z t , t , c ) = ( 1 + β ) ​ ϵ θ ​ ( z t , t , c ) − β ​ ϵ θ ​ ( z t , t , ∅ ) , \hat{\epsilon}_{\beta}(z_{t},t,c)=(1+\beta)\,\epsilon_{\theta}(z_{t},t,c)-\beta\,\epsilon_{\theta}(z_{t},t,\varnothing), (2) where β > 0 \beta>0 is the guidance scale and ∅ \varnothing denotes the null condition. This approximately corresponds to sampling from a sharpened distribution p β ​ ( z 0 ∣ c ) ∝ p ⁡ ( z 0 ) ​ p ​ ( c ∣ z 0 ) β p_{\beta}(z_{0}\mid c)\propto p(z_{0})\,p(c\mid z_{0})^{\beta} , which concentrates probability mass around the dominant modes of the conditional distribution. While this yields sharper and more prompt-faithful images, it systematically suppresses low-density modes, reducing output diversity across images generated from the same prompt. 4 Proposed Method 4.1 Constrained Diversity Maximization on Initial Noise Given a batch of initial latent codes Z T = { z T i } i = 1 B ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 𝟎 , I ) Z_{T}=\{z_{T}^{i}\}_{i=1}^{B}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},I) , we compute one-step Tweedie predictions { z ^ 0 | T i } i = 1 B \{\hat{z}_{0|T}^{i}\}_{i=1}^{B} via Eq. 1 . Even at the initial timestep T T , these predictions capture meaningful semantic structure such as global layout, dominant colors, and object placement [ 2 ] . Since deterministic samplers such as DDIM [ 26 ] define a fixed mapping from initial noise to final image, diversifying Tweedie predictions at t = T t{=}T propagates through the entire generation path without per-step intervention. Our goal is to optimize Z T Z_{T} so that these predictions are maximally diverse while remaining in plausible regions of the data distribution. We formalize diversity through RKHS volume maximization and fidelity through an anchor-based displacement constraint, then combine them via Lagrangian relaxation into a single objective. Experiments on SD1.5, SDXL, and SD3 confirm consistent diversity gains across backbones and samplers, with Pareto analysis showing that λ \lambda enables smooth interpolation between the two objectives. A toy experiment and a spectral analysis ( Proposition 1 ) trace this advantage to its mechanism: repulsion that intensifies where the batch is most collapsed and relaxes once diversity is restored. In downstream few-shot classification, the broader mode coverage translates into statistically significant accuracy gains in the low-data regime. Treating diversity as a property of the whole batch, rather than of its pairs, thus produces image sets that are not only more varied but measurably more useful.
